title: Session 2: Mongoose, MongoDB, Express & React Setup

questions.questionText: What is the role of Mongoose in the context of MongoDB and Node.js?
options: A package that acts as a bridge between Node.js and MongoDB
questions.correctAnswer: A package that acts as a bridge between Node.js and MongoDB
questions.explanation: A package that acts as a bridge between Node.js and MongoDB. Mongoose connects Node.js applications to MongoDB and offers a convenient API for database operations.

questions.questionText: MongoDB is best described as which type of database system?
questions.explanation: A NoSQL database system. MongoDB is a popular NoSQL database offering high performance, scalability and flexibility.

questions.questionText: What is MongoDB Compass?
options: An Integrated Development Environment (IDE) / graphical interface for MongoDB
questions.correctAnswer: An Integrated Development Environment (IDE) / graphical interface for MongoDB
questions.explanation: An Integrated Development Environment (IDE) / graphical interface for MongoDB. Compass is the official graphical user interface (IDE) for MongoDB.

questions.questionText: From which website is the MongoDB Community Server installer downloaded in this session?
questions.explanation: mongodb.com/try/download/community. Step 1 of the MongoDB installation uses https://www.mongodb.com/try/download/community.

questions.questionText: Which MongoDB Community Server version is selected in the guide?
questions.explanation: 6.0.8. The guide selects version 6.0.8 for Windows x64.

questions.questionText: Which platform is chosen when downloading MongoDB in the guide?
questions.explanation: Windows x64. Platform Windows x64 is selected before clicking Download.

questions.questionText: In the Open File - Security Warning dialog, which button starts the MongoDB installation?
questions.explanation: Run. Clicking Run in the dialog box starts the installation process.

questions.questionText: What type of file is the downloaded MongoDB installer in the guide (for example, mongodb-installer.msi)?
options: A compressed archive (.zip) that needs no installer
questions.explanation: A Windows Installer Package (.msi). The installer is a Windows Installer Package with the .msi extension, run by double-clicking it.

questions.questionText: How do you accept the MongoDB Community Server Agreement during setup?
options: Click Cancel and restart the wizard
Check the box accepting the terms in the License Agreement, then click Next
Type 'I agree' in the Service Name field
Skip the screen – it is optional
questions.correctAnswer: Check the box accepting the terms in the License Agreement, then click Next
questions.explanation: Check the box accepting the terms in the License Agreement, then click Next. The EULA screen requires the acceptance box to be ticked before Next.

questions.questionText: Which setup type is selected on the Choose Setup Type screen?
questions.explanation: Complete. The Complete option installs all program features, including the configuration settings.

questions.questionText: On the Service Configuration screen, how is the MongoDB service run?
options: As a local or domain user
It is not installed as a service
questions.explanation: As Network Service user. The guide chooses 'Run service as Network Service user'.

questions.questionText: What is the default service name kept on the Service Configuration screen?
questions.explanation: MongoDB. The service name is left as the default value, MongoDB.

questions.questionText: After the MongoDB installation finishes, which installer screen is displayed next?
questions.explanation: The MongoDB Compass installation screen. The installer offers 'Install MongoDB Compass', and Next proceeds with its installation.

questions.questionText: Which button is clicked on the 'Ready to Install' screen to begin installation with the chosen settings?
questions.explanation: Install. Click Install to begin installation; Back reviews settings, Cancel exits.

questions.questionText: Which button closes the installer at the 'Completing the MongoDB Setup Wizard' screen?
questions.explanation: Finish. Click Finish to exit the Setup Wizard.

questions.questionText: What happens when the MongoDB installation completes?
options: A React app is created automatically
MongoDB Compass launches automatically with a user-friendly dashboard
questions.correctAnswer: MongoDB Compass launches automatically with a user-friendly dashboard
questions.explanation: MongoDB Compass launches automatically with a user-friendly dashboard. Compass launches and shows the 'Welcome to Compass' dashboard.

questions.questionText: Which code editor is used in the guide to set up Mongoose?
questions.explanation: Visual Studio Code (VS Code). Step 1 of Mongoose setup is to open Visual Studio Code.

questions.questionText: What is the name of the root project folder created for the Mongoose set-up?
questions.explanation: MERN. MERN is the root directory for the project.

questions.questionText: What is the name of the folder created inside the MERN folder?
questions.explanation: Session02. Session02 organizes the project files for this session.

questions.questionText: How do you open a terminal window within VS Code?
questions.explanation: View → Terminal. Go to View → Terminal and navigate to the Session02 folder.

questions.questionText: Which command initializes a new Node.js application in the guide?
questions.explanation: npm init -y. npm init -y converts the current folder into a Node.js application.

questions.questionText: Running npm init -y creates which file in the Session02 folder?
questions.explanation: package.json. The package.json file stores project information and dependencies.

questions.questionText: Which command installs the Mongoose package?
questions.explanation: npm install mongoose. The command downloads and installs Mongoose and its dependencies into the project.

questions.questionText: What does the package.json file do in a Node.js project?
questions.explanation: Defines project dependencies and metadata. package.json describes the project and lists its dependencies.

questions.questionText: Which command is used in the guide to build a ReactJS app inside a folder named 'frontend'?
questions.explanation: create-react-app frontend. create-react-app frontend creates the React application within the frontend folder.

questions.questionText: What is the name of the folder in which the React app is built?
questions.explanation: frontend. The ReactJS app is created within a folder named 'frontend'.

questions.questionText: Which command installs the Express framework?
questions.explanation: npm install express. Express is installed using npm install express.

questions.questionText: After installing Express and Mongoose, where are both added?
questions.explanation: The package.json file. Both packages appear as dependencies in package.json.

questions.questionText: Which website is used to download Node.js?
questions.explanation: nodejs.org/en. The guide opens https://nodejs.org/en to download the installer.

questions.questionText: Which edition of Node.js does the guide choose for a stable version?
questions.explanation: Long Term Support (LTS). Choose the LTS edition for stability; 'Current' offers the latest features.

questions.questionText: Node.js is best described as which of the following?
options: An open-source, cross-platform JavaScript runtime environment
questions.correctAnswer: An open-source, cross-platform JavaScript runtime environment
questions.explanation: An open-source, cross-platform JavaScript runtime environment. The Node.js download page describes it exactly this way.

questions.questionText: Who is shown as the Publisher in the Node.js installer security warning?
questions.explanation: OpenJS Foundation. The security warning lists the publisher as OpenJS Foundation.

questions.questionText: How do you accept the Node.js license agreement in the setup wizard?
options: Select the option to accept the terms in the License Agreement
Close the wizard and reopen it
questions.correctAnswer: Select the option to accept the terms in the License Agreement
questions.explanation: Select the option to accept the terms in the License Agreement. Acknowledging the agreement is required before proceeding.

questions.questionText: Which setup option is selected to individually choose each Node.js subcomponent?
questions.explanation: Custom. The Custom option lets you choose each subcomponent individually.

questions.questionText: The 'Tools for Native Modules' screen offers tools to compile native modules. Which tools are mentioned?
options: Python and Visual Studio Build Tools
questions.correctAnswer: Python and Visual Studio Build Tools
questions.explanation: Python and Visual Studio Build Tools. Some npm modules need to be compiled from C/C++, so these tools may be needed.

questions.questionText: Which command navigates to the frontend folder before testing the React app?
questions.explanation: cd .\frontend\. Use cd .\frontend\ in the terminal.

questions.questionText: Which command starts the local development server for the React application?
questions.explanation: npm start. npm start launches the dev server and opens the browser.

questions.questionText: What is displayed in the browser after the React development server starts?
options: A dashboard on localhost with the message to edit src/App.js and save to reload
questions.correctAnswer: A dashboard on localhost with the message to edit src/App.js and save to reload
questions.explanation: A dashboard on localhost with the message to edit src/App.js and save to reload. The default React page tells you to edit src/App.js and save to reload.

questions.questionText: ReactJS applications are commonly built as which type of application for seamless user experiences?
questions.explanation: Single-Page Applications (SPAs). The summary states that React apps are commonly built as SPAs.

questions.questionText: What is the role of Express in a Node.js application?
options: Provides a user interface for the application
questions.explanation: Handles server-side routing and middleware. Express is the web application framework for Node.js handling routing and middleware.

questions.questionText: MongoDB is a relational SQL database system.
questions.explanation: MongoDB is a NoSQL database system.

questions.questionText: Mongoose acts as a bridge between Node.js and MongoDB.
questions.explanation: This is the defining role of Mongoose.

questions.questionText: MongoDB Compass can be installed along with MongoDB Community Server through the installer.
questions.explanation: The installer offers an 'Install MongoDB Compass' option.

questions.questionText: Running npm init -y creates a package.json file in the project folder.
questions.explanation: package.json stores project info and dependencies.

questions.questionText: Express is installed using the command npm install mongoose.
questions.explanation: Express uses npm install express; Mongoose uses npm install mongoose.

questions.questionText: The 'Current' edition of Node.js is the one recommended for a stable version.
questions.explanation: The LTS edition is the stable choice.

questions.questionText: The command npm start launches the local development server for the React app.
questions.explanation: The browser then opens with the default React dashboard.

questions.questionText: Installing Mongoose also downloads its dependencies into the project.
questions.explanation: The install command fetches Mongoose and its dependencies.

questions.questionText: In the guide, the MongoDB service is run as Network Service user with the default service name MongoDB.
questions.explanation: Both settings are kept at the guide's defaults.

questions.questionText: ReactJS applications are commonly built as Multi-Page Applications (MPAs).
questions.explanation: They are commonly built as Single-Page Applications (SPAs).
